yaml:
# W3 fixture: a cache save+restore pair at the lowest TTL the DSL permits.
#
# ttlDays: 1 is the floor, not 0. `0` is silently rewritten to 30
# (internal/agent/orchestrator.go:980-982); `<0` and `>365` are rejected
# (internal/dsl/parse.go:614-619). So 1 is the smallest value that actually
# reaches internal/cache/cache.go:90's
# `ExpiresAt: now.Add(ttlDays * 24h)`.
#
# THE `wipe` STEP IS LOAD-BEARING AND MUST STAY FIRST. The host agent keeps a
# persistent per-job workspace (working<slot>/<job>), so on a second run
# `deps/` would still be there from the first one and "CACHE-HIT" would prove
# nothing about the object store. Wiping before the cache step means a hit can
# only have come from `caches/<b64url(sha256(jobName))>/<b64url(sha256(key))>.tar.zst`.
# examples/jobs/cache.yaml's own header makes the complementary warning — with
# no cache store configured the cache step is a silent no-op — so a fixture
# that merely "passes" proves nothing either way. Read the marker's timestamp:
# on a genuine hit it is the PREVIOUS run's, which no no-op can produce.
apiVersion: unified-cd/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: edge-cache-user
spec:
  native: true
  agentSelector:
    - kind:linux
  steps:
    - name: wipe
      run: |
        rm -rf deps
        echo "wiped; deps present after wipe: $(test -e deps && echo yes || echo no)"

    - name: restore_deps
      cache:
        path: deps/
        key: edge-cache-user-v1
        restoreKeys:
          - edge-cache-user-
        ttlDays: 1

    - name: use_deps
      run: |
        set -e
        if [ -f deps/marker ]; then
          echo "CACHE-HIT"
          echo "marker-planted-at: $(cat deps/marker)"
        else
          echo "CACHE-MISS"
          mkdir -p deps
          date -u +%FT%T.%NZ > deps/marker
          echo "marker-planted-at: $(cat deps/marker)"
        fi
        echo "now: $(date -u +%FT%T.%NZ)"
